cards.title: World Notes: The Real Wardrobe
cards.sub: A real thing behind one of our books
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read with your lens in mind.
text: In The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, the way into Narnia is a wardrobe.
C.S. Lewis really grew up with a big wooden wardrobe. His grandfather, Richard Lewis, made it by hand in the 1800s. It stood in the family’s house in Belfast, and later in Lewis’s home in England.
Today it is in a museum at Wheaton College, in Illinois. Some people think it helped give Lewis the idea for the wardrobe in Narnia.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. Last day! Share your writing, look back at the year, and get your certificate.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: roll word-part words, one last editing pass, and roll spelling words.
transcripts.guide2: Finish your response, look back down the Reading Road, and write to a new 3rd grader.
transcripts.guide3: Give your response a title and share it out loud. Then get your certificate.

notes.wordParts: Word parts I know: -y and -ness mean being something, -ous means full of, -ful means full of, -less means without, un- means not, re- means again.
notes.grammar: Editing checklist: capitals on names and the first word, apostrophes for belonging and joined words, a comma before and/but/so when it joins two complete thoughts, and the right past form, like went.
notes.spelling: Find the base word first. Then check what was added: drop the silent e (hope, hoping), double the last letter (hop, hopping), change y to i (cry, cried), or add -es (box, boxes).
notes.wgrd: Good readers look back at how they have grown. Name one skill that was hard in the fall and is easy for you now.
vocab: doing the right thing even when no one is watching
understanding and sharing the feelings of another person
the ability to keep going after something hard
